title: Quantum circuits of elastic wave equations via Schrödingerisation
abstract: We construct explicit quantum circuits for the velocity-stress formulation of elastic wave equations in homogeneous media using Schrödingerisation. After rewriting the equations in symmetric matrix form(SMF), we use Fourier spectral discretization for source-driven periodic problems and staggered-grid finite differences for Dirichlet, Neumann, and impedance boundary conditions. The Schrödingerisation method transforms any linear PDEs into a system of Schrödinger-type PDEs -with unitary evolution- using the warped phase transformation that maps the equations in one higher dimension. For periodic problems, we develop circuits by combining controlled Fourier-mode rotations. For physical boundaries, interleaved encoding swaps the spatial and field-component registers, enabling a more efficient circuit construction using shift operators. We analyze $p$th-order Trotter-Suzuki formulas and derive splitting-error and CNOT-gate estimates, under the assumptions of smooth auxiliary initialization and solution-state recovery. Comparison with classical partitioned splitting methods identifies a polynomial improvement in spatial-resolution dependence for the quantum state-evolution subroutine. Noiseless circuit simulations of a forced periodic problem and an impedance problem illustrate the constructions and quantify their errors against exact solutions and classical reference computations.
summary: This paper develops explicit quantum circuits to simulate the time evolution of elastic wave equations using the Schrödingerisation method. By mapping the PDEs to unitary quantum evolution, the authors construct circuits for both periodic and physical boundary conditions. The work demonstrates a quantum advantage by achieving a polynomial improvement in spatial resolution scaling over classical simulation techniques.
main_problem: The paper aims to construct explicit quantum circuits to simulate the time evolution governed by the elastic wave equations.
main_result: The authors provide circuits for both periodic and physical boundary conditions, demonstrating a polynomial improvement in spatial-resolution dependence compared to classical methods.
method: The core method is Schrödingerisation, which transforms the linear Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) into a unitary evolution governed by a Schrödinger-type Hamiltonian, which is then decomposed into quantum gates.
model_or_system: The system modeled is the elastic wave equation in homogeneous media, analyzed using the velocity-stress formulation. The evolution is discretized using Fourier spectral methods for periodic domains and staggered-grid finite differences for physical boundaries.
key_observables: Velocity ($v$) and Stress ($\sigma$) fields at a final time $T$; circuit complexity measured in CNOT gates.
important_parameters: The order of the Trotter-Suzuki approximation ($p$); spatial resolution ($d$); time $T$.
main_assumptions: Assumes smooth auxiliary initialization and solution-state recovery for error analysis; the circuit decomposition relies on the exact factorization of the directional evolution operator due to disjoint subspaces.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the quantum circuits for the directional evolution operator $\exp(iA_\ell t)$ for $d=2$ and $d=3$, and show comparisons of simulated velocity and stress fields against exact and classical solutions.
paper_structure: The paper first reviews the elastic wave equations and the Schrödingerisation technique. It then details the circuit construction for periodic systems using controlled rotations, followed by circuits for physical boundaries using interleaved encoding swaps. Finally, it analyzes the complexity and presents numerical comparisons.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, resource-aware quantum algorithm for simulating complex, time-dependent PDEs, which is highly relevant for quantum simulation of many-body dynamics in condensed matter or AMO contexts.
